title: Public-Anchor Drift Adapters for Privacy-Limited Embedding Model Upgrades

raw.stage1:
### Purpose
The contribution's purpose is to enable privacy-preserving embedding model upgrades without access to in-domain data. Paper [3] discusses privacy-preserving model upgrades in image retrieval, specifically addressing the challenge of upgrading models without accessing raw gallery images. While the application domain differs (image retrieval vs. dense retrieval), the purpose of privacy-preserving model upgrades is substantively equivalent. Therefore, the purpose is **covered** by paper [3].

### Mechanism
The contribution introduces the Public-Anchor Drift Adapter (PADA), a lightweight residual MLP trained with a simple MSE objective on paired embeddings from public Wikipedia text, mapping new-model embeddings into the legacy embedding space without requiring in-domain data. Paper [1] presents Drift-Adapter, a learnable transformation layer that maps new queries into the legacy embedding space, enabling embedding model upgrades without re-encoding the corpus. While the specific implementation details differ (e.g., residual MLP vs. unspecified transformation layer), the underlying mechanism — learning a mapping between embedding spaces — is substantively equivalent. Therefore, the mechanism is **covered** by paper [1].

### Evaluation
The contribution evaluates PADA by training on ~5,000 Wikipedia anchor pairs and testing the upgrade scenario (all-distilroberta-v1 → all-mpnet-base-v2) using nDCG@10. Paper [1] evaluates Drift-Adapter in embedding model upgrade scenarios using retrieval metrics (e.g., recall@k). Both papers use a similar evaluation design: embedding model upgrade scenarios validated via retrieval metrics. The specific benchmark instance (Wikipedia anchor pairs, nDCG@10) differs, but the evaluation design is substantively equivalent. Therefore, the evaluation is **covered** by paper [1].

### Domain
The contribution operates in the domain of dense retrieval and embedding model upgrades in vector databases, specifically targeting privacy-sensitive deployments. Papers [5], [6], [7], and [8] all address vector databases and embedding model upgrades in dense retrieval systems. While none explicitly focus on privacy-sensitive deployments, the general application area of dense retrieval and embedding model upgrades in vector databases is well-covered. Therefore, the domain is **covered** by papers [5], [6], [7], and [8].
